answer: An agent economy can weight votes by tokens locked in a vault for 30 days, rather than by account count. A cipher secures access, but creating more keys earns no extra influence: splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still yields only 100 tokens of voting weight. Like adding footprints on a dune, extra identities add no substance. To gain power, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital for the full lock period.
